- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33) in recent days, model tends to overpredict; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently underestimates true values in the 10–15 day horizon; apply a +0.5 to +1.0 point bias correction for this window.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 3–5 day horizon.
- Model shows mean reversion bias: if 3–5 day average is above 70, forecast tends to be too low; if below 65, tends to be too high — apply mean-reversion correction to align with 3-day rolling average.
- Sentiment volatility >0.25 in last 5 days correlates with forecast error; reduce forecast variance by 10–20% for volatile sentiment periods.
